notes.text: The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 30% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the fifth-lowest in the league (a typical team: 39%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Nate Schmidt is on injured reserve and has missed the last 8 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters.
John Marino is day to day and has missed the last 16 games. He is a top-pair defenseman.
Michael Carcone is on injured reserve (upper-body surgery) and missed their last game.
Nick Schmaltz is on injured reserve (lower body injury) and has missed the last 6 games. He is a top-six forward.
Dylan Guenther returned in their last game after missing 6 games. Their recent numbers were built mostly without him.

Quinn Hughes is on injured reserve and has missed the last 2 games. He is one of their most valuable skaters. Brock Faber has taken his spot beside Jonas Brodin. That pair has had 57% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 34:44 together, about what it had with Hughes (56%).

Olli Määttä is out (upper body injury) and has missed the last 4 games. Brock Faber has taken his spot beside Jonas Brodin. That pair has had 47% of the chances at 5-on-5 in 57:53 together, about what it had with Määttä (48%).
Marcus Foligno is no longer killing penalties: 4% of the team’s shorthanded time in 12 games, down from 34% last season.

stakes: The Mammoth go in seventh in the Central with 27 points, 14 points behind the Wild, first in the NHL.

MIN.head: A slightly uphill night for the Wild
MIN.body: Utah has been out-chancing opponents lately, while Minnesota will be without Hughes. Then again, Minnesota has home-ice advantage, and Utah will be without Schmidt. The Wild can tip it if their power play gets going.

UTA.head: The Mammoth start a half-step ahead
UTA.body: Utah has been out-chancing opponents lately, while Minnesota will be without Hughes. Then again, Minnesota has home-ice advantage, and Utah will be without Schmidt. Still, it’s close: the Wild can make it interesting if their power play gets going.

story.head: Sergachev fought last time
paras: The Wild won the teams’ first meeting this season, 3-1 in Utah on Oct 27. The Mammoth (12-10-3) lost 4-2 to Winnipeg on Monday, while the Wild (18-3-5) beat San Jose 5-2 the same night. Going in, the Mammoth are seventh in the Central (tied for 16th in the NHL) and the Wild are first in the NHL.

The Mammoth have played better than their record (.540) says: their chances are worth about .699, and their goaltending has held them back. The Wild’s record (.788) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.640), largely thanks to their goaltending.

The Mammoth (1st) and the Wild (2nd) both let the point shots come and guard the net. The Mammoth rarely get pinned in their own end (1st), but rarely threaten on the penalty kill (31st). The Wild, by contrast, get pinned in their own end on long shifts (32nd). They also have had some of the league’s best goaltending (2nd). Minnesota has allowed 2.19 goals a game, the fewest in the league. Something has to give when the Wild’s shooting runs into the Mammoth’s defense. Beyond that, both teams like to hit, so expect plenty of it.

Clayton Keller (5 G / 24 A / 29 P in 24 GP) leads the Mammoth in scoring, with eight goals in twelve games against Minnesota since 2023-24. Logan Cooley (12 G / 14 A / 26 P in 22 GP) has a team-high twelve goals. Kirill Kaprizov (19 G / 30 A / 49 P in 26 GP) leads the Wild in scoring and is second in the NHL, with 14 points in his last five games.

Karel Vejmelka (6-7-2 / .869 SV% in 15 GS) has had a rough start to the season for Utah, but is expected to start. Jesper Wallstedt (16-2-4 / .923 SV% in 22 GS) has been terrific for Minnesota and is expected to start.

items.text: Last time these two met, there were three fights. For Mikhail Sergachev, it was his first fight since February 2023.

The Mammoth are newly without Michael Carcone, and have been without Nate Schmidt, John Marino and Nick Schmaltz for several games. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Capitals are missing more right now.
Mikhail Sergachev has a point in six straight games against Minnesota, and 10 points in his last six against them.
The Wild are newly without Quinn Hughes, and have been without Olli Määttä since Nov 14.
